status: docs-scoped structured proof; not production runtime authority

principles.atomicTruth: exact profile id + version + executable pattern id
principles.whyDefault: why the hand/event qualifies or is special; player strategy only when separately evidenced
principles.scoreAuthority: derive from exact treatment reference; do not treat learner prose as score authority

facetDefinitions.ordinary-grouped: Qualifying structure uses the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.irregular-hand: Qualifying structure does not use the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.event-defined: The winning event/context is essential to qualification.
facetDefinitions.one-suit: Qualifying suited tiles come from one numbered suit; honours may still be permitted or required.
facetDefinitions.multiple-suits: The qualifying structure explicitly uses more than one numbered suit.
facetDefinitions.pairs: Pairs are an essential structural feature.
facetDefinitions.pungs-kongs: Pungs and/or Kongs are essential structural features.
facetDefinitions.chow-involving: A Chow is required or explicitly permitted by the reviewed variant.
facetDefinitions.honours: Wind and/or Dragon tiles are structurally required.
facetDefinitions.knitted-interleave: Same-number tiles across suits form the defining interleaved structure.
facetDefinitions.green-tiles: Composition is restricted to Green Dragon and the permitted green Bamboo tiles.

examples.presentation: preserve four Wind Pung/Kong group boundaries plus the pair
examples.visibleExplanation: Four Wind Pungs/Kongs plus a pair.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Four Blessings hand: a Pung of East Winds, a Pung of South Winds, a Pung of West Winds, a Pung of North Winds, and a pair of Green Dragons.

examples.presentation: irregular collection; do not create false meld boundaries
examples.visibleExplanation: Every suited 1 and 9, all four Winds, all three Dragons, plus one duplicate.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Thirteen Unique Wonders hand: 1 and 9 of Bamboo, Circles and Characters; East, South, West and North Winds; Red, Green and White Dragons; and a second East Wind.

examples.visibleExplanation: British / Club - Bramhall 2026 example using Green Dragons and green Bamboo tiles, with Pungs and a pair only.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example British / Club - Bramhall 2026 Imperial Jade hand: a Pung of Green Dragons, Pungs of 2 Bamboo, 3 Bamboo and 6 Bamboo, and a pair of 8 Bamboo.

examples.visibleExplanation: Western example showing the permitted 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Thompson and Maloney Imperial Jade hand: a Pung of Green Dragons, a 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow, Pungs of 6 Bamboo and 8 Bamboo, and a pair of 2 Bamboo.

examples.visibleExplanation: One suit from 1 through 9, a second 1, and all four Winds.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Wriggling Snake hand: 1 through 9 Circles, a second 1 Circle, and East, South, West and North Winds.

examples.visibleExplanation: One suit from 1 through 9, all four Winds, and a duplicate of any one tile in that thirteen-tile base; this example duplicates East Wind.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example broader Wriggly Snake hand: 1 through 9 Circles, East, South, West and North Winds, and a second East Wind.

examples.visibleExplanation: Seven pairs made only from Winds, Dragons and suited 1s or 9s.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example All Pair Honours hand: seven pairs using 1 Bamboo, 9 Circles, 1 Character, East Wind, South Wind, Red Dragon and Green Dragon.

examples.visibleExplanation: Seven pairs using one numbered suit, with honours allowed.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Western All Pair hand: pairs of 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 Bamboo, East Winds and Red Dragons.

examples.visibleExplanation: Seven pairs entirely within one numbered suit.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Heavenly Twins hand: seven pairs, using 1 through 7 Circles.

examples.visibleExplanation: Seven distinct pairs. Under Western — T&M, you must win from the wall.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Seven Twins hand: pairs of 1, 3, 5 and 7 Bamboo, 2 Circles, East Winds and Red Dragons. Under these rules, you must win from the wall.

examples.visibleExplanation: East's initial dealt hand is already Mahjong.
examples.accessibleDescription: Heaven's Blessing event sequence: East receives the original deal, the hand is already complete, and East declares Mahjong.

steps: Replacement tile completes a second Kong
examples.visibleExplanation: A linked two-Kong replacement-tile sequence ending in Mahjong.
examples.accessibleDescription: Twofold Fortune event sequence: a Kong is declared, its replacement tile completes a second Kong, the second Kong is declared, and the next replacement tile completes Mahjong.

examples.visibleExplanation: Pungs or Kongs of all three Dragons, plus another set and a pair under BMJA and Western — T&M.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Three Great Scholars hand: Pungs of Red, Green and White Dragons, a Pung of East Winds, and a pair of 5 Circles.

examples.visibleExplanation: Seven same-number pairs across exactly two suits; duplicate pairs are allowed where physical tile copies permit them.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Knitting arrangement showing seven pairs formed from matching numbers across different suits.

examples.visibleExplanation: Four same-number groups across all three suits plus a same-number pair across two suits.
examples.accessibleDescription: Example Triple Knitting arrangement: four same-number three-suit groups, plus one same-number pair using two suits.

examples.visibleExplanation: One suit with three 1s, three 9s, one each 2 through 8, and one extra middle tile in this example.
examples.accessibleDescription: Gates of Heaven tile pattern in Circles: 11123455678999. The extra tile rule depends on the rules you use.

entries.summary: All 13 terminal and honour tile types, plus one extra matching tile.
entries.whatItIs: You need the 1 and 9 from each suit, all four Winds, all three Dragons, and one extra copy of any of those tiles.
entries.whatItMeans: This hand does not use the usual four sets and a pair. It is a fixed group of terminal and honour tiles.
entries.whySpecial: You must collect all 13 required tile types, then pair one of them.
howItWorks: Keep the 1 and 9 of all three suits.
Keep all four Winds and all three Dragons.
Complete one of each of those thirteen tile types.
Use the fourteenth tile to duplicate one of them.

treatmentTeaching.difference: The tile pattern is the same; BMJA scores it under its own rules.
The tile pattern is the same; Western — T&M gives it a different fixed score.
The tile pattern is the same; Club - Bramhall 2026 also requires a concealed hand.
Buzzard calls this hand Thirteen Odd Majors and scores it at the table limit.

watchOutFor: Do not try to split the hand into ordinary Chows and Pungs.
The extra tile can match any one of the 13 required tile types.

entries.summary: Pungs or Kongs of East, South, West and North, plus a pair.
entries.whatItIs: All four sets are Wind Pungs or Kongs. Add any legal pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Every Wind must make a complete set. Simply having all four Winds in the hand is not enough.
howItWorks: Make a Pung or Kong of East Wind.
Do the same for South, West and North.
Complete the hand with a pair.

treatmentTeaching.difference: The hand shape is the same. BMJA uses its own score, with a minimum of 400 or the normal hand score if that is higher.
Shared structure; Thompson & Maloney assigns its own fixed value.
The hand shape is the same; exposed sets score differently under Club - Bramhall 2026.

entries.summary: A hand made from Green Dragons and the green Bamboo tiles. The Chow rule depends on your rules.
entries.whatItIs: Use Green Dragons and Bamboo 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.
entries.whatItMeans: British / BMJA and Club - Bramhall 2026 do not allow a Chow. Western — T&M allows one 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow.
entries.whySpecial: Only a small set of green tiles may be used, so the Chow rule changes which hands count.

variants.label: British / Club - Bramhall 2026 form
variants.definition: Four Pung or Kong groups and a pair, all from Green Dragons and Bamboo 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8. No Chow is allowed.

variants.label: Thompson & Maloney Western form
variants.definition: Use the same green tiles. One 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow is allowed.

entries.summary: 1 to 9 in one suit, all four Winds, and one extra matching tile.
entries.whatItIs: Both Snake hands use the same 13-tile base: 1 to 9 in one suit plus all four Winds.
entries.whatItMeans: Wriggling Snake pairs the suited 1. Wriggly Snake may pair any tile from the 13-tile base.
entries.whySpecial: The whole hand is a fixed tile pattern, not normal sets.

variants.label: Wriggling Snake
variants.definition: 1-9 in one suit, all four Winds, with the suited 1 duplicated.

variants.label: Wriggly Snake
variants.definition: 1-9 in one suit, all four Winds, with any one tile in that thirteen-tile base duplicated.

entries.summary: Several special hands use seven pairs, but the tile and winning rules differ.
entries.whatItIs: Compare All Pair Honours, All Pair, Heavenly Twins and Seven Twins.
entries.whatItMeans: All four use pairs. They differ in which tiles may be paired and, for Seven Twins, how the hand is won.
entries.whySpecial: Seven-pair hands do not use the usual four sets and a pair.

variants.label: All Pair Honours
variants.definition: Seven pairs, each made from a Wind, Dragon, or suited 1/9.

variants.label: All Pair
variants.relation: name-collision with All Pair Honours; neither predicate contains the other
variants.definition: Seven pairs using at most one numbered suit, with honours allowed.

variants.label: Heavenly Twins
variants.definition: Seven pairs entirely in one numbered suit, without honours.

variants.label: Seven Twins
variants.relation: distinct effective qualification because the winning method matters
variants.definition: Seven distinct loose pairs. You must win from the wall under these rules.

entries.summary: East is dealt a complete winning hand before play starts.
entries.whatItIs: East’s original 14 tiles already make Mahjong.
entries.whatItMeans: BMJA calls this Heaven’s Blessing. Buzzard calls it Original Hand and also records the historical names Hand from Heaven and Natural Winning.
entries.whySpecial: East wins from the original deal, before any ordinary draw or discard.
howItWorks: The hand is already a legal Mahjong.
The win is recorded as the original-deal event.
entries.referenceNote: The Buzzard source says East wins with a complete hand from the original deal. BMJA uses the phrase “Mah Jong in original deal”; the historical names do not prove that all rules use the same event.

entries.summary: Two linked Kong replacement draws end with Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: A replacement tile completes a second Kong, then the next replacement tile completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItMeans: The order of the two Kongs and replacement draws matters. The final hand shape alone is not enough.
entries.whySpecial: The win depends on a specific sequence of events.
howItWorks: Its replacement tile completes a second Kong.
The next replacement tile completes Mahjong.

entries.summary: All versions use Pungs or Kongs of all three Dragons. The fourth set and pair rules differ.
entries.whatItIs: Make a set of Red, Green and White Dragons, then complete the hand under the selected rules.
entries.whatItMeans: BMJA and Western — T&M require another Pung or Kong. Club - Bramhall 2026 also allows a Chow when the fourth set and pair use the same numbered suit. Buzzard allows any legal fourth set and pair.
entries.whySpecial: The three Dragon sets are shared; the rest of the hand decides which version you have.

variants.label: Three Great Scholars — BMJA / Thompson & Maloney
variants.definition: All three Dragon Pung/Kongs plus a fourth Pung/Kong and a pair.

variants.label: Three Great Scholars — Club - Bramhall 2026
variants.definition: All three Dragon Pung/Kongs; the fourth meld may be a Chow, Pung or Kong, and it and the pair use the same numbered suit.

variants.label: Three Dragons — Buzzard 2000
variants.definition: Pungs or Kongs of all three Dragons, plus a legal fourth set and pair.

entries.referenceNote: Under Buzzard 2000, a hand that misses this win condition may still affect the table score.

entries.summary: Seven same-number pairs made across exactly two suits.
entries.whatItIs: Match the same number across two different suits to make seven pairs.
entries.whatItMeans: Only two numbered suits may be used. You do not make normal Chows, Pungs or Kongs.
entries.whySpecial: The whole hand is built from cross-suit pairs.

variants.label: Two-suit Knitting
variants.definition: Seven pairs of matching numbers across exactly two suits. The score and exposure rules depend on the rules you use.

entries.summary: Four same-number groups using all three suits, plus one same-number pair across two suits.
entries.whatItIs: Each three-tile group uses the same number once in Bamboo, Circles and Characters. Add one same-number pair using two suits.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand is a 14-tile pattern, not normal melds.
entries.whySpecial: Every group follows the same cross-suit knitting idea.

variants.label: Triple Knitting
variants.definition: Four groups with the same number in all three suits, plus a same-number pair across two suits. The score and exposure rules depend on your rules.

entries.displayName: Gates of Heaven / Calling Nine Tile Hand
entries.summary: A one-suit 1112345678999 base. The allowed extra tile depends on the rules.
entries.whatItIs: Start with three 1s, three 9s and one each of 2 to 8, all in one suit.
entries.whatItMeans: BMJA, Western — T&M and Buzzard use different rules for the extra tile and how the hand is completed.
entries.whySpecial: The base is tightly fixed, so the exact winning tile matters.

variants.label: BMJA Gates of Heaven
variants.definition: Uses the middle-rank duplicate skeleton and BMJA-specific completion/how the hand was won logic.

variants.label: Western Gates of Heaven
variants.definition: Use one suit: 1112345678999, with one extra tile from 2 to 8. Keep the hand concealed.

variants.label: Calling Nine Tile Hand
variants.definition: Starts from the 1112345678999 base and permits any same-suit 1-9 tile as the completing extra tile.
